approve.risk: Once you approve it, this device gets full access to your AgentRe account as you, including running arbitrary code and commands. Only approve devices you trust.
approve.verify: Check that this code matches exactly what the device shows

add.kindLabel: Which kind of device are you adding?
add.kindHint: No need to add a browser — the one you are using is already in the list

install.agentredDesc: agentred is the long-running process that executes tasks; once it is installed it can sign in to your account.
install.serviceLabel: Register it as a background service so it stays up after you close the terminal
install.desktopTitle: Install the Agentre desktop app on that computer
install.desktopDesc: The desktop app has agentred built in; once installed, sign in to the same account from the app.
install.downloadBody: Download the installer for that platform from GitHub Releases (macOS .dmg / Windows .exe / Linux .deb).

login.agentredTitle: Sign it in to this account
login.agentredDesc: Run this command on that machine. The server address is already this console's own address, so you can copy it as is.
login.agentredTip1: The command prints a line reading User code: XXXXXX — that is the six-character device code.
login.agentredTip2: It also tries to open a browser; servers usually have none, so bring that code back here instead.
login.agentredTip3: The device code expires; run the command again if it does. The approval screen counts down the time left.
login.desktopTitle: Sign in to the same account from the desktop app
login.desktopDesc: Open Agentre and go to Settings → Remote → Sign in, using this console as the server address.
login.desktopTip1: The desktop app shows a six-character device code and tries to open a browser to authorize it.
login.desktopTip2: If no browser opens, or you would rather approve it on this computer, bring that code to the next step.
login.desktopTip3: The device code expires; start over from the desktop app if it does. The approval screen counts down the time left.

code.handoff: Submitting opens the approval screen, where you check the code against the device and approve it.
